findings.title: Denial cache can deny access after permissions are granted, with no invalidation path
findings.body: The new permDenialCache is checked before anything else in Check() and is only ever written (never deleted/invalidated). When a user is denied a resource, the denial is cached for shortCacheTTL (30s). If the user's permissions are subsequently changed (e.g. an admin grants access to that dashboard, or the user is added to a role/team), the denial entry still takes precedence over the freshly-recomputed permission state: the code returns Allowed=false immediately at the top of Check() without ever consulting the (possibly updated) permission cache or DB. Unlike the permission cache, which gets overwritten on the next DB query, there is no mechanism anywhere in this PR to evict a denial entry, so a granted user can be locked out for up to 30 seconds. If any existing permission-invalidation hooks exist they do not clear this new cache.

findings.title: userPermDenialCacheKey is ambiguous due to '_' separators
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey builds the cache key by concatenating action, name and parent with '_' separators: namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent. Because the resource name and parent folder UID are free-form strings that may themselves contain underscores, two distinct requests can produce the same key (e.g. name="a", parent="b_c" vs name="a_b", parent="c"). A denial cached for one resource would then be incorrectly returned for a different resource, causing wrongful denial. Use a separator that cannot appear in the components or hash/escape the parts.

findings.title: permissionCacheUsage 'miss' metric is emitted even when the cache lookup failed for non-miss reasons
findings.body: In Check(), getCachedIdentityPermissions can return an error for reasons other than a cache miss — notably GetUserIdentifiers failing with a DB error, or an unsupported identity type (which returns a hard error). In all those cases the code still increments permissionCacheUsage with hit="false" and then proceeds to getIdentityPermissions, which will also fail. This distorts the cache-hit-ratio metric: genuine backend errors are counted as cache misses, making the cache look less effective than it is during incidents.

findings.title: Dead cacheHit field and removed cache-hit test case in TestService_getUserPermissions
findings.body: The 'should return permissions from cache if available' test case was deleted, but the testCase struct still has the cacheHit field and the test body still contains the 'if tc.cacheHit' branch asserting store.calls == 1. Since no remaining test case sets cacheHit=true, this code is dead and the caching behavior of getUserPermissions/getIdentityPermissions (that a permCache hit avoids the store call) is no longer covered at that level. Either remove the dead field/branch or restore a cache-hit case so the cache path stays tested.
